samples.summary: Adding `readOnly` to the mount-effect deps cannot fire: the share role is resolved once and never revalidated, so revoking/downgrading a share link mid-session still leaves a fully writable docs editor attached
samples.evidence:
The new comment (docs-view.tsx:572-579) states the dep protects "a session that *loses* write authority while open (a share link re-resolving from `editor` to `viewer`)". Tracing the only producer of that prop: `SharedDocsLayout` computes `const readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"` (shared-document.tsx:322) from `resolved`, which `SharedDocumentByToken` sets from a single `resolveShareLink(token).then(setResolved)` inside a `useEffect(..., [token])` (shared-document.tsx:1086-1102). There is no polling, no react-query refetch, no re-resolution on focus or on socket event — so `readOnly` is constant for the lifetime of the mount and the new dep never re-runs the effect. The owner route (docs-detail.tsx:280) passes no `readOnly` at all.

Why this is an authorization gap rather than a cosmetic one: `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:38-42` states outright that "the server-side check behind it — the Yorkie auth webhook — ships in shadow mode by default (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE`), so with the default configuration this flag is the write boundary rather than a convenience in front of one", and `packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:111-119` confirms it: when `enforce` is false a denial is logged and `ALLOW` is returned. Attack: an owner revokes or downgrades an `editor` share link while the holder's tab is open. The holder's client never re-resolves the link, so `readOnly` stays false and `initialize()` keeps handing the raw `YorkieDocStore` (editor.ts:1075) to the editor; because the webhook never returns 401/403 in shadow mode, the Yorkie SDK is also never prompted to refresh its token via `authTokenInjector` (shared-document.tsx:1000), so the stale grant is never re-checked either. The holder keeps writing to the shared document indefinitely after revocation.

The defect is the absence of any revalidation of `ResolvedShareLink.role` (or of a server-side enforcement the client can rely on), which the new dep is written as if it had.

samples.summary: The new `this.readOnly` re-check documents itself as re-reading the permission "at the moment of the write", but `readOnly` is immutable per instance, so the guard is a constant and the comment overstates the protection it gives
samples.evidence: The added comment (text-editor.ts:4253-4260) claims the re-check exists so that "the permission this session is allowed to exercise is the one that decides — not the one that held when the shortcut was pressed and the clipboard prompt went up." But `readOnly` is a private field set only in the constructor (`private readOnly = false;` at text-editor.ts:191, `this.readOnly = readOnly;` at :719) and there is no setter anywhere in packages/docs/src (grep for `setReadOnly|readOnly =` returns only doc-canvas.ts:157/159 and these two lines). Its value at the moment of the resumed write is therefore always identical to its value at keydown, and the keydown path is already gated: `handleKeyDown` returns for every non-navigation key under `if (this.readOnly)` at text-editor.ts:1096-1112, before the Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+V branch at :1373-1375 is ever reached. The only state that *can* change across the clipboard await is `disposed`, which is what an editor rebuilt for a new permission actually sets (text-editor.ts:6069 via editor.ts:4392). Impact is limited to the comment's accuracy — a future reader may take it as evidence that permission changes are tracked on a live instance (they are not) and skip a real gate on that basis. The guard itself is harmless defence-in-depth and worth keeping; the justification should be corrected.

samples.summary: `deferPaste`, the other write that resumes after an await, still re-validates only `disposed` while the delta adds a `readOnly` re-check to `pastePlainTextFromClipboard` — the two async-resume paths now disagree
samples.evidence: The delta's own comment calls the plain-text path "the only one that resumes", but `deferPaste` (text-editor.ts:1604-1622) also awaits (`yieldToPaintedFrame()` at :1606) and then writes, guarded only by `if (!this.disposed) job();` at :1609. Its callers do gate on `readOnly` synchronously (`handlePaste` at :1672, `pasteContent` at :1661), and — as in the finding above — `readOnly` cannot change on a live instance, so there is no exploitable gap today; a viewer-mounted editor is additionally writing through `readOnlyDocStore` (editor.ts:1075). Raised only because the delta establishes a re-validate-permission-on-resume convention at one of the two sites and not the other, which invites the reverse conclusion later if `readOnly` ever becomes mutable.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `readOnly` for the docs share route is derived from `resolved.role` (shared-document.tsx:322,364), and `resolved` is set by exactly one `resolveShareLink(token).then(setResolved)` inside `useEffect(..., [token])` (shared-document.tsx:1086-1102) — a repo-wide grep for `setResolved` finds no other writer, and greps for setInterval/visibilitychange/focus/refetchInterval/refetchOnWindowFocus and any share-link revoked/updated event across packages/frontend/src turn up nothing on this path (only notifications, documents-list polling, view analytics, pick-files). So the newly added `readOnly` dep at docs-view.tsx:581 cannot fire for a mid-session downgrade, contrary to the comment at :572-579. The server-side check that would compensate does re-read the link per RPC (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:212-220, editor role required for `rw`), but it is gated on `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true'` (:100-101) and returns ALLOW while logging `[shadow] would deny` otherwise (:111-119); the default is documented as shadow/allow-everything (self-hosting.md:185, backend/README.md:101, sharing.md:208), and read-only.ts:38-42 states the client flag is therefore the write boundary. Because no 401/403 is ever returned in shadow mode, the Yorkie SDK is never prompted to re-mint via authTokenInjector (shared-document.tsx:1000), so the stale grant is never re-checked there either. Net effect in the stock configuration: an owner who revokes or downgrades an editor share link does not stop the holder's open tab from continuing to write to the shared document — a real authorization gap (major) in the security lane. The non-default enforce flag is a mitigation the finding already accounts for, not a counterexample.

finding.summary: The async-resumed clipboard write re-validates lifecycle state but not write permission, and `readOnly` is never re-armed for a mounted editor
finding.evidence: `pastePlainTextFromClipboard()` resumes after `await navigator.clipboard.readText()` and now re-checks two invariants — `if (this.disposed || this.pasting) return;` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4254) — with the diff's own comment noting the read can take arbitrarily long because a permission prompt is a user interaction. The one invariant it does not re-check is whether this session may still write. That would be moot if `readOnly` could not change, but it is captured once at construction (`TextEditor` ctor arg, text-editor.ts:717-719) and the mount effect that builds the store and calls `initialize(container, store, theme, readOnly)` (docs-view.tsx:359) has dependency list `[didMount, doc]` (docs-view.tsx:573) — `readOnly` is absent. So a share-link role that resolves to `viewer` on a refetch (`const readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"`, packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:322) flips the surrounding UI to view-only while the mounted editor keeps its stale writable flag and every `readOnly` guard inside `TextEditor` keeps answering false. Attack shape: a user with edit access starts a Cmd+Shift+V (or simply keeps the tab open) while the owner revokes edit access; the resumed write, and every subsequent keystroke, still reaches `YorkieDocStore` and syncs to all peers. This matters more than a typical client-side flag because `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:38-42` records that the server-side Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow mode by default (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE`), i.e. the client flag *is* the write boundary in the default configuration. I could not confirm that the share-link resolution actually refetches within a mount, so confidence is low; the defect is pre-existing rather than introduced here, but the diff is precisely the change that decides which invariants an async-resumed write revalidates, which is why I raise it on this guard.

verdict.reason:
The finding rests on two absence claims, and both are contradicted by the working tree.

(1) "The one invariant it does not re-check is whether this session may still write." False. `pastePlainTextFromClipboard()` resumes at packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4261 with `if (this.disposed || this.pasting || this.readOnly) return;` — `readOnly` IS re-read at the moment of the write, and the surrounding comment (4255-4260) states exactly that rationale ("it is read here, at the moment of the write, so the permission this session is allowed to exercise is the one that decides — not the one that held when the shortcut was pressed"). The reviewer quoted the guard as `if (this.disposed || this.pasting) return;` at line 4254; line 4254 is a blank comment line and the actual guard includes the readOnly term.

(2) "the mount effect ... has dependency list `[didMount, doc]` (docs-view.tsx:573) — `readOnly` is absent." False. The dep list is at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:581 and reads `}, [didMount, doc, readOnly]);`. Line 573 is inside the preceding comment block (572-579) which explicitly explains that `readOnly` is load-bearing in the deps precisely for the scenario the finding describes: "a session that *loses* write authority while open (a share link re-resolving from `editor` to `viewer`) kept a fully writable editor ... Listing it rebuilds the editor against the current permission." Because `readOnly` is a dependency, a flip to viewer runs the cleanup at 549-571, which calls `editor.dispose()` (565; sets `this.disposed = true` at text-editor.ts:6069) and then re-runs `initialize(container, store, theme, readOnly)` (359) with the new value — so both the in-flight resumed paste (blocked by `disposed` and `readOnly` at 4261) and every subsequent keystroke run against a re-armed editor.

The attack chain therefore has no unguarded step in this repository.
